hook: The Netherlands is low and flat, and much of it lies below sea level. By the old idea of environmental determinism, the sea should decide where the Dutch can live. Instead, over centuries, they built dikes and pumped out water, and about a sixth of the country is land taken from the sea. The environment set the limit; people chose what to do about it.

prereq.why: Site is the physical character of the spot itself.

prereq.q: Which kind of data is an interview with a farmer?

figure.caption: Environmental determinism said the environment decides; possibilism says it sets limits and people choose.

chain.cause: The physical environment sets limits, such as steep slopes, dry land or a low coast
chain.effect: people face choices about how to use the land and its natural resources

chain.cause: People use culture and technology to adapt or reshape the land
chain.effect: land use changes: fields on slopes, land taken from the sea, cities in deserts

chain.cause: Resources are used faster than they can be replaced
chain.effect: the land, water or fish run down, which is not sustainable

ideas: Natural resources are things from nature that people use. Renewable ones (sunlight, wind, fish, water) can replace themselves; nonrenewable ones (oil, coal) are used up.
Land use is how people use an area of land: forest, farms, homes, roads, factories.
Sustainability means using resources so that people now meet their needs without harming the ability of future people to meet theirs.
Environmental determinism said the environment decides human behavior; it was rejected and was used to justify European rule. Possibilism says the environment sets limits and people choose.

misconception.wrong: Possibilism means people can do anything, whatever the environment.
misconception.right: Possibilism still says the environment sets limits. People choose among the options it offers, using their culture and technology, and their choices can have costs, as at the Aral Sea.

summary: People and the environment shape each other. Natural resources can be renewable or nonrenewable, and how people use land changes the environment. Sustainability means using resources so they last for future users. Geographers once held environmental determinism, the idea that the environment decides how people live; they rejected it as wrong and as a cover for unequal rule, and moved to possibilism: the environment sets limits, and people choose.
